subject: ela
intro: Each item gives you a compound or complex sentence, or a short pair of sentences. Your job is to analyze the pronouns: fix an inappropriate shift in number or person, or resolve a vague pronoun that could point to two different people. Rewrite the sentence so it follows standard English and so every pronoun clearly matches its antecedent.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'When a student forgets their lunch, they can borrow money from the front office.' Rewrite the sentence so the pronouns agree in number with their antecedent. Keep the meaning the same.
items.answer: When students forget their lunch, they can borrow money from the front office.

steps: Find the antecedent and the pronouns. The antecedent 'a student' is singular, but the pronouns 'their' and 'they' are plural, so the number does not match.
The easiest fix that keeps a natural, plural-sounding pronoun is to make the antecedent plural.
Change 'a student' to 'students,' which now agrees with 'their' and 'they.'
Corrected sentence: 'When students forget their lunch, they can borrow money from the front office.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'If a runner trains every morning, you will see a big improvement by spring.' Rewrite the sentence to fix the inappropriate shift in person.
items.answer: If a runner trains every morning, he or she will see a big improvement by spring.

steps: Identify the point of view. The sentence begins in the third person with 'a runner' but shifts to the second person with 'you.'
A pronoun should stay in the same person as its antecedent throughout the sentence.
Replace the second-person 'you' with a third-person pronoun that matches the singular 'a runner.'
Corrected sentence: 'If a runner trains every morning, he or she will see a big improvement by spring.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Carla told Jada that she had been chosen for the lead role.' This sentence is unclear. Explain why, then rewrite it so it clearly means that Jada was chosen.
items.answer: The pronoun 'she' is vague because it could refer to either Carla or Jada. Corrected: 'Carla told Jada that Jada had been chosen for the lead role.'

steps: Locate the pronoun and its possible antecedents. 'She' could point to Carla or to Jada, so the reference is ambiguous.
Because the sentence is meant to say Jada was chosen, replace the vague 'she' with the name 'Jada.'
Corrected sentence: 'Carla told Jada that Jada had been chosen for the lead role.'
Now the reader knows exactly who was chosen.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Each member of the boys' team brought their own water bottle to practice.' Rewrite the sentence so the pronoun agrees in number with its singular antecedent 'each member.'
items.answer: Each member of the boys' team brought his own water bottle to practice.

steps: Identify the antecedent. 'Each member' is singular, even though the phrase 'boys' team' is nearby, so the pronoun must be singular.
The plural pronoun 'their' does not agree in number with the singular 'each member.'
Because the team is the boys' team, the matching singular pronoun is 'his.'
Corrected sentence: 'Each member of the boys' team brought his own water bottle to practice.'

items.prompt: Read these two sentences: 'Mr. Lopez handed the report to Mr. Diaz. He looked very pleased with the results.' Rewrite the second sentence so it is clear that Mr. Diaz looked pleased.
items.answer: Mr. Lopez handed the report to Mr. Diaz. Mr. Diaz looked very pleased with the results.

steps: Find the vague pronoun. 'He' in the second sentence could mean Mr. Lopez or Mr. Diaz.
Since the sentence should say Mr. Diaz looked pleased, replace 'He' with the name 'Mr. Diaz.'
Corrected: 'Mr. Lopez handed the report to Mr. Diaz. Mr. Diaz looked very pleased with the results.'
Now the antecedent is clear and there is only one possible reading.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'A good citizen votes in local elections, and you should also attend town meetings.' Rewrite the sentence to remove the inappropriate shift in person.
items.answer: A good citizen votes in local elections, and he or she should also attend town meetings.

steps: Notice the point of view. The first part uses the third person, 'a good citizen,' but the second part switches to the second person, 'you.'
Keep one consistent person throughout the sentence.
Replace 'you' with a third-person pronoun that matches the singular antecedent 'a good citizen.'
Corrected sentence: 'A good citizen votes in local elections, and he or she should also attend town meetings.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'The teachers told the parents that they needed to sign the permission slips.' This sentence is unclear. Rewrite it so it clearly means the parents needed to sign.
items.answer: The teachers told the parents that the parents needed to sign the permission slips.

steps: Find the ambiguous pronoun. 'They' could refer to the teachers or the parents.
Because the parents are the ones who sign permission slips, that is the intended meaning.
Replace the vague 'they' with the noun 'the parents.'
Corrected sentence: 'The teachers told the parents that the parents needed to sign the permission slips.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'When someone joins the chess club, they must bring their own board, but you also get a free practice guide.' Rewrite the sentence so the pronouns stay consistent in both number and person with the singular antecedent 'someone.'
items.answer: When someone joins the chess club, he or she must bring his or her own board, but he or she also gets a free practice guide.

steps: Identify the antecedent and the pronouns. 'Someone' is singular, but 'they' and 'their' are plural, and 'you' is second person, so there are two problems.
Fix the number first: change 'they' and 'their' to singular 'he or she' and 'his or her' to match 'someone.'
Fix the person next: change the second-person 'you' to the third-person 'he or she,' and adjust 'get' to 'gets' for agreement.
Corrected sentence: 'When someone joins the chess club, he or she must bring his or her own board, but he or she also gets a free practice guide.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Devon and me wanted to enter the science fair, so the teacher gave the entry forms to him and I.' Rewrite the sentence using the correct pronoun case in both the subject and the object.
items.answer: Devon and I wanted to enter the science fair, so the teacher gave the entry forms to him and me.

steps: Check the subject. 'Devon and me' is the subject doing the wanting, so it needs the subjective case: 'Devon and I.'
Check the object. 'Him and I' receives the forms, so it needs the objective case: 'him and me.'
Test each pronoun alone: 'I wanted' and 'gave the forms to me' both sound correct.
Corrected sentence: 'Devon and I wanted to enter the science fair, so the teacher gave the entry forms to him and me.'

items.prompt: Read these two sentences: 'The coach praised the captain during the meeting. She said the season had gone well.' Rewrite the second sentence so it clearly means the coach made the statement.
items.answer: The coach praised the captain during the meeting. The coach said the season had gone well.

steps: Find the vague pronoun. 'She' in the second sentence could refer to the coach or the captain.
Since the sentence should say the coach made the statement, that is the intended antecedent.
Replace the ambiguous 'She' with 'The coach.'
Corrected: 'The coach praised the captain during the meeting. The coach said the season had gone well.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'If a driver wants a parking pass, they must fill out the form, and you must pay a small fee.' Rewrite the sentence so the pronouns agree in number and stay in the third person to match 'a driver.'
items.answer: If a driver wants a parking pass, he or she must fill out the form and pay a small fee.

steps: Identify the antecedent. 'A driver' is singular and third person.
The pronoun 'they' is plural, so it does not agree in number, and 'you' is second person, so it does not agree in person.
Replace 'they' with the singular 'he or she,' and remove the second-person clause by combining the actions under the same subject.
Corrected sentence: 'If a driver wants a parking pass, he or she must fill out the form and pay a small fee.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Aisha reminded Bianca that her project was due on Friday.' This sentence is unclear. Rewrite it so it clearly means Bianca's project was due.
items.answer: Aisha reminded Bianca that Bianca's project was due on Friday.

steps: Find the vague pronoun. The possessive 'her' could refer to Aisha or Bianca.
Because the sentence should say Bianca's project was due, that is the intended owner.
Replace 'her' with the possessive name 'Bianca's.'
Corrected sentence: 'Aisha reminded Bianca that Bianca's project was due on Friday.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'Anyone who wants extra credit should see me after class, and they should bring their notebook.' Rewrite the sentence so the pronouns agree in number with the singular antecedent 'anyone.'
items.answer: Anyone who wants extra credit should see me after class and should bring his or her notebook.

steps: Identify the antecedent. 'Anyone' is a singular indefinite pronoun.
The pronouns 'they' and 'their' are plural, so they do not agree in number with 'anyone.'
Replace 'they should bring their notebook' with a singular version that matches 'anyone.'
Corrected sentence: 'Anyone who wants extra credit should see me after class and should bring his or her notebook.'

items.prompt: Read these two sentences: 'Marcus passed the basketball to Jordan, and then he scored the winning point. Everyone cheered.' Rewrite the first sentence so it clearly means that Jordan scored.
items.answer: Marcus passed the basketball to Jordan, and then Jordan scored the winning point. Everyone cheered.

steps: Find the vague pronoun. 'He' could refer to Marcus or Jordan.
Since the sentence should say Jordan scored, that is the intended antecedent.
Replace the ambiguous 'he' with the name 'Jordan.'
Corrected sentence: 'Marcus passed the basketball to Jordan, and then Jordan scored the winning point. Everyone cheered.'

items.prompt: Read the sentence: 'A scientist records data carefully because you cannot trust results that they did not check twice.' Rewrite the sentence so it stays in the third person and the pronoun agrees in number with the singular 'a scientist.'
items.answer: A scientist records data carefully because he or she cannot trust results that he or she did not check twice.

steps: Identify the antecedent. 'A scientist' is singular and third person.
The sentence shifts to the second person with 'you' and to the plural with 'they,' so both the person and the number are inconsistent.
Replace 'you' and 'they' with the singular, third-person 'he or she' to match 'a scientist.'
Corrected sentence: 'A scientist records data carefully because he or she cannot trust results that he or she did not check twice.'
